task.description: Re-check of prior FAIL: confirm AC3 four-role InstancesAdvanceTimer matrix is now genuinely covered, sanity-check the pre-existing rustc-toolchain baseline failure, and confirm no other item regressed.

result.summary:
AC3 gap is fixed. Read test/letflow/api/authorization_test.exs lines 237-257 directly: the new describe block 'ISS-0389 AC3 -- InstancesAdvanceTimer role matrix (all four named roles)' contains four tests with genuine, unambiguous assertion bodies (not just titles): 'PROCESS_OPERATOR grants InstancesAdvanceTimer' -> assert Authorization.role_allows?(:PROCESS_OPERATOR, :InstancesAdvanceTimer); 'TASK_WORKER denies InstancesAdvanceTimer' -> refute role_allows?(:TASK_WORKER, ...); 'AGENT_RUNNER denies InstancesAdvanceTimer' -> refute role_allows?(:AGENT_RUNNER, ...); 'PLATFORM_ADMIN grants InstancesAdvanceTimer' -> assert role_allows?(:PLATFORM_ADMIN, ...). All four design-doc AC3 role/permission pairs are directly asserted at unit level. Prior FAIL is resolved.

Accepted ORCH's independently-verified aggregate as given (3243 total tests across 8 partitions, 3241 passed, 2 pre-existing environment-only failures, zero new failures). Sanity-checked the rustc dependency myself by reading test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs: 'a matching rust pin reports OK...' (line 274) and 'a mismatched rust pin reports a MISMATCH row...' (line 289) both call running_rust_version() -> running_rust_raw() -> System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"], ...) directly (line 69), with no rescue around the System.cmd call itself -- when `rustc` is absent from PATH, System.cmd raises ErlangError :enoent before the surrounding case/pattern-match can run. This confirms the failure genuinely depends on a rustc binary being present and is a real sandbox/environment gap, not a regression this branch introduced (the branch's diff only touches authorization.ex, routers/instances.ex, scheduler.ex, and their tests/specs -- confirmed via `git diff b5fe974c..1fde5fe7 --stat`, no toolchain-check files touched).

Confirmed via `git diff 8b321a59..1fde5fe7 -- test/letflow/api/authorization_test.exs` that only the new AC3 describe block was added since my prior review; nothing else in the branch changed after my prior PASS on AC1, AC2, AC4-AC10, the fixture bug fixes, mutation-test methodology, or test/specs/ISS-0389.md, so none of those items are reopened.
result.lesson_for_future_runs: The '444/446' and '418/419' figures reported earlier by TEST-DESIGNER/ORCH in this run were not fabricated -- they were real single-partition 'Result: N passed' summary lines from mix letflow.check.test's N-way parallel partitioning, mislabeled in narration as 'full suite' totals. The underlying test content and pass/fail counts were accurate for that partition; the error was aggregation/reporting, not invention of numbers. Future agents narrating this task's output must sum all partitions' result lines (this run: 474+344+431+446+419+324+423+382 = 3243) before calling a number 'full suite,' and should flag explicitly which partition a quoted count came from if not aggregating.
result.verdict: PASS -- AC3 genuinely covered with direct, correctly-asserted role-matrix tests; baseline rustc failures are confirmed environment-only and pre-existing; no other item regressed. Routing to TEST-RUNNER for the formal Step Final confirmation run.
